text:
Linh: Heads-up — I'm seeing a recurring memory "plateau then pulse" pattern on the on-prem rack when serving very long contexts (>60k tokens). Latency spikes correlate with an eviction burst.
Tom: Can you paste the runtime trace + a short repro?
Linh: paste from the instance: ```
[2026-03-17T21:12:04Z] runtime: kv_frame_reserve id=847 size=3.8MB
[2026-03-17T21:12:04Z] runtime: kv_frame_commit id=847 lifetime=300s
[2026-03-17T21:17:06Z] pager: reclaim start count=1 reclaimed=1.2GB
[2026-03-17T21:17:06Z] runtime: eviction_pulse reason=frag_threshold
[2026-03-17T21:17:07Z] metrics: p95=420ms p99=1.1s
```
Linh: This only happens on the private on-prem cluster. Dedicated/cloud and hosted don't show the same periodic reclaim.
Maya: Two quick suspects: kernel/mmap flags + hugepage config differences, and kv->reuse config drift between environments. What kernel versions are we comparing?
Akshat: On-prem node: 5.10.129, no THP, jemalloc 5.3.0. Hosted/dedicated: 6.1.x with THP enabled + jemalloc patched with our cf-allocator fixes.
Tom: That already smells like fragmentation. Without THP and with older jemalloc we see more small-slot fragmentation and slab blowup for long-lived KV frames.
Paul: Also remember VPC path on private uses jumbo-off MTU=1500 and our gRPC windowing differs — could increase the number of smaller KV update packets, altering lifetime patterns. Not sure if that would cause reclaim pulses though.
Rachel: Observed customer impact: p95 up ~120ms during pulses; one Dedicated customer hit SLO on their high-concurrency workload when running on the on-prem appliance.
sre-bot: ALERT: EVICT_PULSE_HIGH on on-prem-rack-3 — 6 occurrences in last 2h.
Akshat: Quick experiment: toggled kv.reuse=true on one on-prem node and increased batch target from 8->16. After ~30m the amplitude of the memory pulses dropped ~40%. Could be reuse policy + batching interaction.
Linh: Nice. Can you share the commands/flags you changed?
Akshat: ```
--kv.reuse=true --batching.target=16 --allocator.tcache=off
# restart runtime only, keep kernel the same
```
Tom: We'll need a controlled repro to isolate kernel vs allocator vs config. Suggest: 1) run perf + pagewalk traces on onprem, 2) run same workload on a dedicated node with old jemalloc to see if allocator is primary, 3) try kernel 6.1 build in staging on onprem hardware.
Maya: Also add a synthetic long-context benchmark that steadily grows context to 120k tokens and holds KV frames for >10 minutes to reproduce the reclaim rhythm.
Paul: Deployment constraints: for private we can't do kernel upgrades without customer approval. We should therefore focus short-term on config parity (kv.reuse, batch target, jemalloc flags) and a runtime fallback that reduces tail latency during a reclaim (e.g., serve throttling or micro-batching).
Rachel: Actionable items: 
- Akshat to produce a 1-click repro and the config diff (kv.reuse, batching.target, allocator flags) — due EOD.
- Tom + Maya to run perf traces comparing jemalloc versions on dedicated vs onprem next day.
- SRE to add an alert that correlates KV-frame churn with p99 latency.
- Engineering to draft a short KB for customers with on-prem appliances explaining recommended kernel/allocator settings.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for on-prem-staging after detection of elevated p99 (reason: automated fallback).
Linh: Thanks — I'll follow up with raw perf logs and a small repro script. If we can show config parity fixes the issue, we can push a constrained runtime patch without kernel changes.
Tom: +1. If kernel ends up being necessary we'll coordinate with the ops/customer success teams for upgrade windows.
Maya: I'll add a regression test to the CI long-context suite so we don't regress this again.
Akshat: Uploading the profiling tarball now: link: https://internal/redwood/perf/2410000000/onprem-repro.tar.gz
Linh: Great, leaving the thread open for updates. :mag:
